comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C4, C59-C62) regarding Hap4's role downstream of Snf1. Both evaluations support the genetic evidence, with OpenEval rating as SUPPORTED and peer review also rating as SUPPORTED. Both acknowledge the necessity and sufficiency experiments demonstrating Hap4 mediates Snf1's effect on MP import.

Perfect claim overlap (C91-C97) on disease-relevant proteins. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong validation across multiple readouts. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, accepting the experimental observations but questioning the physiological relevance and contribution of MAGIC to overall misfolded protein removal using model substrates.

Perfect claim overlap (C57-C58) on negative results ruling out Mig1/Mig2 transcriptional repressors. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these help define the pathway by focusing on transcriptional activators, and peer review accepts these findings without challenge.

Perfect claim overlap (C38-C41) on technical controls for the spGFP system. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges the control addresses potential artifacts, and peer review accepts the validity of the reporter system without raising concerns.

Perfect claim overlap (C106-C109) on the synthesized model. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the model integrates multiple lines of evidence. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the key message is important but stating that evidence for physiological relevance of MAGIC and its contribution to overall cellular proteostasis remains incomplete.

High overlap (C80-C84, C86-C89) on protective effects in yeast. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive evidence linking Snf1 to cellular fitness protection. Peer review accepts these findings about protective effects without challenge, noting the fluorescent assays support the claims well.

High overlap (C49-C54) on control experiments ruling out alternative explanations. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the systematic approach and sound logic. Peer review accepts these controls without question, stating findings from these assays support the claims well.

High overlap (C5, C64, C66-C69, C74) on substrate competition mechanism. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite noting some inference and incomplete molecular details. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'it remains unclear by which mechanism Snf1 impacts on MAGIC' and whether it involves competition, indicating the mechanistic interpretation involves speculation.

Moderate overlap (C2, C34-C35, C42) on genome-wide screen identifying Snf1. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes robust validation with multiple approaches and statistical significance. Peer review acknowledges the screen findings and role of Snf1, describing the experimental data using fluorescent assays as convincing. Peer review also includes C56 not in OpenEval R1.

Moderate overlap (C44-C47) on AMPK conservation in mammalian cells. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting pharmacological validation and appropriate controls. Peer review R5 combines these claims with human cell data (C99-C102) and rates as SUPPORTED, accepting AMPK's protective role across species.

Moderate overlap (C99-C102) on AMPK protection in human cells with disease-relevant proteins. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes multiple readouts with appropriate controls and cautious mechanistic conclusions. Peer review R5 combines these with yeast AMPK data (C44-C47) and accepts the protective role in both yeast and human cells.

Moderate overlap (C70-C71) on alternative import pathways for MPs. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes claims about TOM complex conformation (C77-C79) not in peer R10. Peer review accepts this finding as part of the mechanistic investigation supporting the competition model.

Partial overlap (C77-C79) on TOM complex conformation affecting MP import. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with some speculation about dimeric TOM preference. Peer review R3 addresses broader mechanism (C5, C64, C66-C69, C74, C77-C79) and rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the mechanism is clear or involves competition.

OpenEval identifies claims C115-C117 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative inferences about physiological tolerance levels and connections to caloric restriction that extend beyond experimental data. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims.

OpenEval identifies claim C121 as UNCERTAIN, noting it is a speculative therapeutic suggestion requiring substantial additional validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this therapeutic speculation, though peer concerns about physiological relevance are related.

Peer review R7 addresses claims C1, C13-C14, C16, C25-C27 about MAGIC pathway's physiological relevance, rating as UNCERTAIN due to lack of quantitative flux information and unclear contribution to overall proteostasis. No corresponding OpenEval result specifically evaluates these foundational claims about the MAGIC pathway itself.
